evidence.excerpt:
Agentic memory systems give LLMs persistent
memory by extracting experience into text and
retrieving it at query time, but the model itself
doesn't evolve: however many interactions it
has had, it starts each query the same. Extrac-
tion errors compound, implicit cross-session
patterns that no single fragment states cannot
be surfaced, and the construction cost grows
with every conversation. Fine-tuning on past in-
teractions does change the weights, but requires
backpropagation at serving time and degrades
on long histories. We introduce CLAM (Car-
ried Latent Adapter Memory), which combines
the strengths of both: a recurrent hypernetwork
performsparametric consolidation, compiling
a stream of session activations into a low-rank
adapter in a single forward pass with no gra-
dient steps and no language-model generation
calls, while a complementaryepisodic buffer
supplies verbatim detail

than extraction systems that spend 12–464 gen-

mation the episodic channel cannot supply rather
than a better-indexed copy of it.Contributions.

conversations, LongMemEval a few hundred ques-
tions), so we build one with a fully automated
six-stage pipeline (Figure 2), driven throughout
by Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (Dubey et al., 2024). It
follows the LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2025) and
LoCoMo (Maharana et al., 2024) recipes (planted
evidence, distractor sessions, memory taxonomies)
but is automated end-to-end.

evidence.excerpt:
We evaluate onLoCoMo(Maharana et al., 2024)
andLongMemEval-S(Wu et al., 2025), which
are standard LLM memory evaluation benchmarks.
On LoCoMo we use the 1,540 questions of the
four answerable categories (the adversarial cate-
gory is excluded). For LongMemEval-S we sam-
ple 30 questions per type (seed 0) and evaluate on
the 173 answerable ones; its 7 abstention items
are excluded, as LoCoMo's adversarial category
is. Because the parametric baselines train at test
time, they are compared on a 180-question Lo-
CoMo subset and on the same LongMemEval-S
questions. Every system is run on the same three
open base models:Gemma-2-2B(Gemma Team
et al., 2024),Qwen3-4B(Yang et al., 2025) and
Mistral-7B(Jiang et al., 2023). On both bench-
marks the episodic buffer retrieves the same unit:
a session split on turn boundaries into pieces of at
most 1,800 characters.

degenerate to ideal. With an oracle buffer, which

p<10−3); on Mistral, already at 79%, it ties (+0.1).

cumulated preferences, rather than a better-indexed

evidence.excerpt:
CLAM is evaluated on two English conversational-
memory benchmarks with base models of 2–7 B
parameters; behavior at larger scale, in other lan-
guages, and on non-conversational histories such as
documents or code remains to be established. The
consolidated adapter is a fixed-size store, though
better results can be expected from scaling the
adapter rank and the hypernetwork's parameter
count. Finally, the hypernetwork is trained once per
base model on synthetic multi-session data; trans-
ferring a trained hypernetwork to an unseen base
model without retraining is outside the scope of
this work.
Ethics Statement
This work uses two public benchmarks, LoCoMo
and LongMemEval-S, together with a synthetic
corpus generated from fictional personas. Both
benchmarks, the open base models and the baseline
implementations are used in accordance with their
respective licences and intended research

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The paper re-grades 2,880 judgments with three additional judges, including cross-family Qwen3 models, and reports high agreement with no sign flips; Cover-EM, a deterministic string-containment metric, also preserves the headline ordering.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical gains in accuracy, latency, and memory construction costs are well-aligned with the presented data and supported by bootstrap confidence intervals. Cross-evaluator checks and exact-match substring metrics (Cover-EM) confirm the stability of the comparative results.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation covers two standard long-term memory benchmarks (LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S) across three model scales (2B to 7B parameters) against 12 baselines spanning agentic and test-time training paradigms. Extensive ablations validate the complementary nature of the consolidation channel and episodic buffer, including oracle buffer and failure-mode analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations are corroborated using three independent LLM judges (including the cross-family Qwen3-30B and Qwen3-8B) as well as the deterministic, non-neural Cover-EM string containment metric.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Accuracy assessed by an automated LLM judge (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct) on standard LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Offline context-distillation training using cross-entropy loss against full-context teacher answers generated via Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct on synthetic multi-session data.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly delineate limitations, including evaluation restricted to English conversational benchmarks, models scaled up to 7B parameters, a fixed-size adapter representation, and hypernetwork training specific to each base model architecture.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is described thoroughly, detailing the Perceiver-based read, carry (gated recurrence), and decode stages alongside the context-distillation training objective. The multi-stage synthetic data generation pipeline used to train the hypernetwork is fully elaborated.
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution addresses a well-defined efficiency and architectural bottleneck in LLM long-term memory with a novel yet sound method. The experimental validation is extensive, incorporating appropriate baselines, controls, ablations, and evaluator independence checks.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces CLAM (Carried Latent Adapter Memory), a dual-channel memory architecture for LLMs combining a recurrent hypernetwork that maps conversation history into a low-rank adapter via a single forward pass with an episodic text buffer for verbatim retrieval.
